headline: Ratchet & Clank's PAL v2.00 reaches 99.44% matched code
summary: Ratchet & Clank's PAL v2.00 rises from 98.48% to 99.44% matched code, with 5,104 of 5,117 functions in the project's progress report. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game. New C includes the Pyrocitor, Suck Cannon beam, hero-item updates and an Orxon sliding platform (#127, #129, #131). Catalogue-boundary repairs and classifying a level object-processing routine as handwritten assembly also change what the report counts.
highlights: The Orxon sliding platform implementation lands in #131 with PAL v1.00 and Japanese map entries. Draft #130 closes without merging, but supplies the approach used in the landed version.
The map-reveal function remains assembly after its pure-C attempt differs from the original (#127).
Declarations and shared views gain more readable names, including library names for core routines (#126).
